items.title: ICT, Digital India & e-Governance Models
items.body:
## ICT — nature & scope

- **ICT** = convergence of **information technology** (computing, data) and **communication technology** (telecom, internet, networks). It underpins banking, education, health, commerce, agriculture and public administration.

## Digital India (launched 1 July 2015, MeitY)

Umbrella programme with **nine pillars** and three vision areas (infrastructure as a utility, governance & services on demand, digital empowerment).

| Nine pillars (indicative) |
|---|
| Broadband Highways · Universal Access to Mobile Connectivity · Public Internet Access |
| e-Governance (reforming govt through tech) · **e-Kranti** (electronic service delivery) |
| Information for All · Electronics Manufacturing · IT for Jobs · Early Harvest Programmes |

## e-Governance interaction models

| Model | Meaning | Example |
|---|---|---|
| G2C | Government-to-Citizen | DigiLocker, UMANG |
| G2B | Government-to-Business | GeM, e-procurement |
| G2G | Government-to-Government | API Setu data exchange |
| G2E | Government-to-Employee | payroll/HR portals |

## Key delivery platforms

- **UMANG** — single app for many government services; **DigiLocker** — verified digital documents; **e-Sign** — Aadhaar-based e-signature; **API Setu** — open-API interoperability layer.
keyPoints: ICT = convergence of information technology (computing) and communication technology (telecom/internet).
Digital India launched 1 July 2015 by MeitY, built on nine pillars.
e-Kranti is the electronic-service-delivery pillar of Digital India.
e-Governance models: G2C (citizen), G2B (business), G2G (government), G2E (employee).
UMANG = unified services app; DigiLocker = verified digital documents; e-Sign = Aadhaar e-signature; API Setu = open-API interoperability.
items.mnemonic: Models 'C-B-G-E' = Citizen, Business, Government, Employee — the four 'who' of e-governance.
items.source: MeitY / PIB — Digital India programme & e-Governance models

items.title: India Stack & Digital Public Infrastructure
items.body:
## India Stack — layered digital public infrastructure (DPI)

A set of **open APIs** built around identity, payments and data, enabling presence-less, paperless and cashless service delivery.

| Layer | Component | Role |
|---|---|---|
| Identity | **Aadhaar** | Unique digital identity / e-KYC |
| Payments | **UPI** | Real-time interoperable retail payments |
| Data | **DigiLocker**, **Account Aggregator** | Verified documents; consent-based data sharing |
| Commerce | **ONDC** | Open network democratising e-commerce |
| Health | **CoWIN / ABDM** | Vaccination & digital health records |

## UPI — scale (2024-25)

- Operated by **NPCI** (RBI-promoted); launched 2016.
- **World's largest real-time retail payment system by volume**; monthly transactions crossed the **16-billion** mark in 2024-25, forming a dominant share of retail digital payments.
- Internationally linked (e.g., Singapore's PayNow), extending cross-border remittance.

## Why DPI matters

- Lowers cost of service delivery, expands **financial inclusion**, and enables direct benefit transfers (DBT) with reduced leakage.
keyPoints: India Stack = open-API digital public infrastructure across identity, payments and data.
Layers: Aadhaar (identity), UPI (payments), DigiLocker & Account Aggregator (data), ONDC (commerce), CoWIN (health).
UPI is operated by NPCI, launched 2016, and is the world's largest real-time retail payment system by volume.
Monthly UPI volumes crossed 16 billion transactions in 2024-25.
Account Aggregator enables consent-based sharing of financial data; ONDC is an open e-commerce network, not a single company's app.
items.source: MeitY — India Stack / DPI; NPCI — UPI statistics 2024-25

items.title: Data Protection & Cyber Law — DPDP Act 2023, Rules 2025 & IT Act 2000
items.body:
## Digital Personal Data Protection (DPDP) Act, 2023

- India's **first dedicated data-protection law**, enacted August 2023, following the *Puttaswamy* (2017) right-to-privacy judgment.
- **Key actors:** Data Principal (the individual), Data Fiduciary (who decides purpose/means of processing), Significant Data Fiduciary (higher-obligation entities).
- **Data Protection Board of India** — adjudicates breaches; penalties **up to ₹250 crore** per instance.
- **Rights:** access, correction, erasure, grievance redressal, nomination. **Children's data** (<18) needs verifiable parental consent.
- **DPDP Rules, 2025** — notified in 2025; operationalise consent managers, security safeguards, breach notification and the Board's functioning.

## Information Technology (IT) Act, 2000

- India's **primary cyber law** for e-commerce and cyber offences; substantially **amended in 2008**.
- **Section 66A** (penalising 'offensive' messages) was **struck down** by the Supreme Court in *Shreya Singhal v. Union of India* (2015) for violating free speech.
- Other key sections: 43A (data-breach compensation), 69 (interception), 70/70A/70B (protected systems, NCIIPC, CERT-In), 79 (intermediary safe harbour).
keyPoints: DPDP Act 2023 is India's first dedicated data-protection law; DPDP Rules were notified in 2025.
DPDP establishes the Data Protection Board of India; penalties up to ₹250 crore per instance.
DPDP roles: Data Principal (individual), Data Fiduciary, Significant Data Fiduciary; children's data needs parental consent.
IT Act 2000 is India's primary cyber law, amended in 2008.
Section 66A was struck down by the SC in Shreya Singhal v. Union of India (2015).
items.mnemonic: DPDP roles = 'Principal owns, Fiduciary processes' — the individual vs the data handler.
items.source: MeitY / PIB — DPDP Act 2023 & Rules 2025; IT Act 2000; Shreya Singhal (2015)

items.title: Cyber Security Architecture & Citizen Redress
items.body:
## Institutional architecture

| Body | Role | Anchor |
|---|---|---|
| **CERT-In** | National nodal agency for cyber incident response | MeitY; IT Act **Sec 70B** |
| **NCIIPC** | Protects **Critical Information Infrastructure (CII)** | NTRO; IT Act **Sec 70A** |
| **Cyber Swachhta Kendra** | Botnet-cleaning & malware analysis | Under CERT-In |
| **I4C** | Cyber-crime coordination & reporting portal | Ministry of Home Affairs |

- **National Cyber Security Policy 2013** — first national policy; aimed at a secure cyber ecosystem and a skilled workforce.
- **CERT-In 2022 directions** — report specified incidents **within 6 hours**; retain logs 180 days; KYC/data retention for VPN & cloud providers.

## Common cyber threats

- **Phishing** (credential-stealing fraud), **ransomware** (file-encrypting extortion), **DDoS** (traffic flooding), **man-in-the-middle** (intercepting communications).

## Citizen redress

- **National Cybercrime Reporting Portal** (cybercrime.gov.in), **helpline 1930**, and **CFCFRMS** (Citizen Financial Cyber Fraud Reporting and Management System) for rapid reporting and freezing of defrauded funds.
keyPoints: CERT-In (under MeitY, Sec 70B) is the national cyber-incident response agency; NCIIPC (under NTRO, Sec 70A) protects Critical Information Infrastructure.
CERT-In's 2022 directions mandate reporting specified cyber incidents within 6 hours.
Cyber Swachhta Kendra is CERT-In's botnet-cleaning centre; National Cyber Security Policy was adopted in 2013.
I4C (under MHA) runs the National Cybercrime Reporting Portal (cybercrime.gov.in) and helpline 1930.
CFCFRMS enables rapid reporting to freeze fraudulently transferred money.
Common threats: phishing, ransomware, DDoS and man-in-the-middle attacks.
items.source: CERT-In cyber-security handbook; NCIIPC; I4C / MHA

items.title: Emerging-Tech Missions — AI, 5G/6G, Quantum, Semiconductors, Supercomputing
items.body:
## IndiaAI Mission (approved 2024)

- Outlay ~**₹10,372 crore** over 5 years (MeitY). Seven pillars: **Compute Capacity** (GPUs), **Innovation Centre**, **Datasets Platform (AIKosh)**, **Application Development**, **FutureSkills**, **Startup Financing**, **Safe & Trusted AI**.
- **Deepfakes / AI governance:** MeitY advisories under the IT Rules 2021 require labelling/traceability of AI-generated content; a dedicated AI law is under debate.

## Connectivity & quantum

- **5G** launched **October 2022**; rolled out across all districts within ~2 years.
- **Bharat 6G Vision** (2023) targets India among global 6G leaders (patents, standards) by ~2030.
- **National Quantum Mission** (approved 2023, ~₹6,003 crore) — quantum computing, **communication (quantum-secure/QKD)**, sensing and materials.

## Hardware missions

- **India Semiconductor Mission** (₹76,000 crore): approved units at **Dholera (Gujarat)** — India's first commercial fab (Tata–PSMC), **Sanand (Gujarat)** (Micron and others), and **Jagiroad/Morigaon (Assam)** (Tata OSAT).
- **National Supercomputing Mission** (2015, C-DAC): the **PARAM** series; **PARAM Rudra** supercomputers dedicated to the nation in 2024.
keyPoints: IndiaAI Mission (2024) has ~₹10,372 crore outlay; pillars include compute capacity, AIKosh datasets, FutureSkills and Safe & Trusted AI.
MeitY advisories address deepfakes/AI-generated content under IT Rules 2021, pending dedicated regulation.
5G launched October 2022; Bharat 6G Vision (2023) targets 6G leadership by ~2030.
National Quantum Mission (2023, ~₹6,003 cr) supports quantum-secure communication.
India Semiconductor Mission (₹76,000 cr): fabs/units at Dholera & Sanand (Gujarat) and Jagiroad/Morigaon (Assam).
National Supercomputing Mission's PARAM Rudra supercomputers were dedicated in 2024 (C-DAC).
items.source: MeitY / PIB — IndiaAI, Semicon India; DoT — 5G/6G; DST — National Quantum Mission; C-DAC — NSM

items.title: Connectivity Backbone & Andhra Pradesh e-Governance
items.body:
## National connectivity & cloud backbone

| Initiative | Purpose |
|---|---|
| **BharatNet** | Optical-fibre broadband to all gram panchayats (rural backbone) |
| **PM-WANI** | Public Wi-Fi hotspots for last-mile access |
| **Common Service Centres (CSC)** | Rural digital access points delivering G2C services |
| **MeghRaj (GI Cloud)** | Government cloud-computing services & empanelled data centres |

## Andhra Pradesh — e-governance leadership

- **Real Time Governance Society (RTGS)** — runs a **Real Time Governance Centre** integrating department data for real-time monitoring of schemes and grievance redress.
- **e-Pragati** — AP's **enterprise-architecture platform** integrating departmental services into a single digital backbone.
- **Praja Sadhikara Survey** — a household **socio-economic data-collection** exercise linking citizen data to services.
- **Mana Mitra** — **WhatsApp-based governance**: citizens access many government services and downloadable certificates directly via a dedicated WhatsApp number, delivered through RTGS.

## Mains angle

- AP illustrates the shift from portal-based to **chat-based, whole-of-government** service delivery, raising both **access** gains and **data-privacy/DPDP-compliance** questions.
keyPoints: BharatNet delivers fibre broadband to gram panchayats; PM-WANI provides public Wi-Fi; CSCs are rural G2C delivery points.
MeghRaj (GI Cloud) is MeitY's government cloud-computing initiative.
AP's Real Time Governance Society (RTGS) runs a real-time centre for scheme monitoring and grievance redress.
e-Pragati is AP's enterprise-architecture platform integrating departmental services.
Praja Sadhikara Survey was a household socio-economic data-collection exercise.
Mana Mitra delivers AP government services and certificates via WhatsApp through RTGS.
items.source: MeitY / DoT — BharatNet, PM-WANI, CSC, MeghRaj; AP Real Time Governance Society; AP IT & e-Governance Dept

items.title: Emerging Digital Technologies — Blockchain, Web 3.0, Cloud & Communication Tech
items.body:
## Blockchain, crypto-assets & Web 3.0

- **Blockchain** = a **distributed, decentralised public ledger** replicated across nodes; records are **immutable** and validated by **consensus** (Proof-of-Work / Proof-of-Stake). No single user controls it, yet everyone can inspect it (a **permissionless** chain lets anyone build apps on it without permission).
- Not limited to cryptocurrency — supports **smart contracts** (self-executing code, e.g. Ethereum), supply-chain tracking, land records.
- **Cryptocurrency** (e.g. Bitcoin) is **fungible** (each unit interchangeable). An **NFT (Non-Fungible Token)** is a **unique** cryptographic token on a blockchain representing a specific digital/physical asset; being non-fungible it is **not** used as an equivalent medium of exchange.
- **Web 3.0** = a decentralised web where users **control their own data**, blockchain-based social networks are possible, and services are run by users collectively rather than a single corporation.

## Cloud service models

| Model | User gets | Example |
|---|---|---|
| **IaaS** | Raw compute/storage/network | AWS EC2 |
| **PaaS** | Platform to build/deploy apps | Google App Engine |
| **SaaS** | Ready software over the internet | **Gmail / Outlook / Yahoo Mail** |

- In **SaaS**, users can often customise the interface and data fields and access data from mobile devices.

## Communication technologies

| Tech | Key fact |
|---|---|
| **RFID** | Radio-frequency tags — short-range identification |
| **NFC** | Contactless via EM radio fields; works only at **~4 cm**; can use **encryption** |
| **WLAN / Bluetooth** | Short-range wireless networking |
| **Li-Fi (VLC)** | Uses **visible light (375–780 nm)** as medium; **many times faster than Wi-Fi**; no EM interference |
| **4G LTE vs VoLTE** | Both are 4G; **VoLTE = Voice over LTE** (carries voice as data over the LTE network) |
| **Project Loon** | Google balloon-based **wireless internet** for remote areas |

## AI — present capabilities

- Present-state AI can already do **disease diagnosis, text-to-speech, content generation** (stories/songs), and optimise **industrial energy use**; it cannot wirelessly transmit electrical energy.
keyPoints: Blockchain is a decentralised, immutable public ledger validated by consensus; permissionless chains let anyone build apps and it is not limited to cryptocurrency.
NFTs are unique (non-fungible) tokens on a blockchain, unlike fungible cryptocurrency; they are not a medium of exchange.
Web 3.0 = decentralised web where users own their data and services are user-run, not corporation-run.
Cloud models: IaaS (infrastructure), PaaS (platform), SaaS (software, e.g. Gmail/Outlook).
NFC works only within ~4 cm and can use encryption; RFID/WLAN/Bluetooth are short-range technologies.
Li-Fi/VLC uses visible light (375–780 nm), is faster than Wi-Fi and has no EM interference.
VoLTE = Voice over LTE (both 4G); Project Loon = balloon-based wireless internet.
items.source: NITI Aayog/MeitY primers on Blockchain & DPI; NIST cloud definition; UPSC-standard S&T references (verified Sep 2026)
